predecessors.name: Dvaravati
predecessors.text: Lavo had been 'one of the supra-regional centres of the Dvaravati mandalas'; Kalavarnadisharaja 'succeeded at Nakhon Pathom in 641' and in 648 'transferred the political centre to the newly founded…

successors.name: Ayutthaya Kingdom
successors.text: 'Lavo was annexed into Ayutthaya in 1388'; Ramesuan retook Ayutthaya from Thong Lan in 1388, bringing 'Ayutthaya and Lavo under one ruler'

ledger.x: 927: the war with Haripunjaya ends as Lavo falls to Tambralinga.

928: Tambralinga annexes Lavo. the page's '[...] left it open to annexation by Tambralinga from the south in 928'; King Jivaka 'occupied Lavo in 927-928 and appointed his son Kampoch'; infobox 'Tambralinga vassal: 927-946'.

946: Tambralinga's hold on Lavo ends. the infobox 'Tambralinga vassal: 927-946' and the table's 'As a tributary state of Tambralinga' (Kampoch, 930-946?); the infobox then reads 'Angkor vassal: 946-1052' and 'Fall of Ayodhyapura: 946', and Lavo 'was devastated from the east in 946 and 1001'.
1006: Angkor takes Lavo under a Khmer governor.
1052: Lavo returns to a ruler of its own.
1082: Narai I moves the capital to Ayodhya.
1106: a new line takes the Lavapura seat.
1181: Jayavarman VII places Lavo under Angkor.
1351: Ayutthaya is founded out of Lavo's land round Ayodhya.
1375: Lavo cedes a further border strip to Ayutthaya.

wars.name: Lavo-Haripunjaya war (925-927)
wars.outcome: 'Battles between Lavo and Haripunjaya are recorded from 925 to 927'; the Lavo king Uchitthaka Chakkawat defended against Rathasatkara of Haripunjaya.

wars.name: Tambralinga's conquest of Lavo (927-928)
wars.outcome: King Jivaka (Suchitra) 'occupied Lavo in 927-928', appointed his son Kampoch, and held it as a tributary 930-946; the page's '[...] left it open to annexation by Tambralinga from the south in 928'.

wars.name: Angkorian conquest of Lavo (1001-1014)
wars.outcome: Suryavarman I's troops destroyed Lavo after the nine-year civil war at Angkor (infobox 1001; table 'around 1005'); Lakshmipativarman governed from 1006; the K.1198 stele is dated 1014 and one reading puts the conquest 'between 1011 and 1014'.

wars.name: Haripunjaya's capture of Lavo (1052)
wars.outcome: 'Haripunjaya's Thamikaraj, with Suphannabhum's help, took Lavo' in 1052 and installed his brother Chandrachota as king (1052-1069).

wars.name: Lavo's northward attacks on Haripunjaya (12th century)
wars.outcome: Lopburi, held by a Mon-Tai clan from Chaliang, 'marched north several times without success' in the twelfth century; no border moved.

wars.name: Angkor's return to Lavapura under Jayavarman VII (1181-1196)
wars.outcome: A governor, Narupatidnavarman, was appointed in 1181; the Prasat Tor inscription records a defeat of a western monarch in 1189/90 or 1195/96.

wars.name: Lopburi-Suphanburi rivalry (1370-1388)
wars.outcome: Borommarachathirat I of Suphanburi took Ayutthaya from Ramesuan in 1370 ('Lopburi and Suphanburi rivalry: 1370-1409'); Ramesuan recovered it from Thong Lan in 1388, bringing 'Ayutthaya and Lavo under one ruler'; in 1408 Intharacha retook Ayutthaya for the…

certainty.note: Lavo was a mandala; no page opened gives a boundary.
